topics.name: HR System Architecture
topics.description: ServiceNow HR plugins, HR table structure, and application scoping.

introduction.overview: The HR System Architecture domain covers the foundational technical components of ServiceNow HR Service Delivery, including plugin dependencies, the HR-specific table structure, and how application scoping works within the HR applications.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain represents 30% of the CIS-HR exam. Questions cover HR plugin activation and dependencies, the HR case and employee tables, lifecycle event tables, and how scoped applications interact with HR functionality.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the HR Core plugin and its dependencies, the sn_hr_core_case table for HR cases, employee tables and their relationships, and how HR scoped applications extend the base functionality while maintaining security boundaries.
introduction.examTips: HR plugins must be activated in the correct order. The HR table structure extends the task table for cases. Know which tables are HR-specific vs platform tables. Scoped applications can extend HR functionality while respecting security.

topics.name: Core HR Applications & Employee Center
topics.description: Users, groups, skills, roles, assignment rules, HR services, catalog items, record producers, and Employee Center branding.

introduction.overview: This domain covers the core HR applications including HR services, catalog items for employee requests, and the Employee Center portal. It also includes configuration of users, groups, roles, and assignment rules for routing HR cases.
introduction.whyItMatters: Core HR Applications represents 30% of the exam. Expect questions on HR service definitions, HR catalog item configuration, record producers for case creation, Employee Center setup and branding, and assignment rule configuration.
introduction.keyConcepts: Master HR service configuration which defines what HR offers to employees. Understand how HR catalog items and record producers work together for employee self-service. Know Employee Center layout, branding, and persona-based content targeting.
introduction.examTips: HR services group related catalog items. Record producers create HR cases from portal forms. Employee Center uses personas to target content. Assignment rules route cases based on criteria like department or location.

topics.name: HR Journeys & Lifecycle Events
topics.description: Lifecycle events, journeys, activity sets, trigger conditions, activities, audience, and activity field mappings.

introduction.overview: HR Journeys and Lifecycle Events enable organizations to automate and guide employees through major transitions like onboarding, transfers, and offboarding. Journeys provide a consumer-grade experience while lifecycle events automate the underlying processes.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain is 20% of the exam. Questions focus on lifecycle event configuration, journey creation and customization, activity sets and activities, trigger conditions, audience targeting, and field mapping for dynamic content.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the relationship between lifecycle events (backend automation) and journeys (frontend experience). Master activity sets, activity types, trigger conditions, audience configuration, and how field mappings personalize journey content.
introduction.examTips: Lifecycle events trigger journeys for employees. Activity sets group related tasks. Activities can be manual or automated. Trigger conditions determine when activities execute. Audience controls who sees specific content.

topics.name: Security & Data Protection
topics.description: Platform security, role-based security, contextual security, delegated developer role, and HR data protection.

introduction.overview: HR Security covers the multiple layers of security in ServiceNow HR applications, including platform-level security, role-based access, contextual security for sensitive employee data, and the delegated developer pattern for controlled customization.
introduction.whyItMatters: Security and Data Protection is 20% of the exam. Questions cover ACL configuration for HR data, role-based access patterns, contextual security for manager-employee relationships, HR data protection requirements, and the delegated developer role.
introduction.keyConcepts: Master the three security layers: platform ACLs, role-based access, and contextual security. Understand how contextual security enables managers to see their direct reports' data. Know the delegated developer role for controlled HR customizations.
introduction.examTips: HR data is sensitive and requires multiple security layers. Contextual security uses relationships (like manager) for access decisions. The delegated developer role allows HR admins to make limited customizations safely.
